The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with a large dark brown/gray lesion in the center featuring concentric rings, with some yellowing on one side. The concentric ring pattern is very prominent.

Let me read the part index first, then start checking reference images.

Leaf is the affected part. From the 18 possible classes, leaf candidates are: Early_Blight, Late_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Gray_Mold, Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

The concentric ring pattern strongly suggests Early Blight. Let me view references one at a time.

This Early Blight reference shows multiple small dark lesions with yellowing - somewhat similar but different from the single large concentric-ring lesion in the test. Let me check another Early Blight reference.
Now let me check Septoria Leaf Blotch.
Septoria shows many small spots - doesn't match. Let me check Late Blight.
Microscopic image - not useful. Let me check Late Blight leaf 50 and Gray Mold.
Late Blight shows grayish irregular patches - no concentric rings, doesn't match. Let me check Gray Mold.
Gray Mold shows large tan necrotic areas without concentric rings - doesn't match. Let me check the third Early Blight reference.
This CDDM_1020 Early Blight shows multiple lesions without a single clear concentric ring lesion. The test image has ONE large target-like lesion. Let me check Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.
TSWV shows bronzing with many tiny spots - doesn't match. I have 1 view remaining. Let me check Verticillium Wilt.

Verticillium Wilt shows wilting/yellowing without focal lesions - doesn't match.

**Summary of all 8 views:**
1. Early_Blight/Bugwood_19 - multiple dark lesions, some yellowing
2. Early_Blight/CDDM_1004 - gray background, dark marginal lesions with yellowing
3. Septoria/CDDM_1006 - many tiny round spots, no rings
4. Late_Blight/Bugwood_10 - microscope image (not useful)
5. Late_Blight/Bugwood_50 - grayish irregular patches, no rings
6. Gray_Mold/Bugwood_27 - large tan necrotic areas, no rings
7. Early_Blight/CDDM_1020 - gray background, multiple dark lesions
8. TSWV/Bugwood_10 - bronzing with tiny spots
9. Verticillium_Wilt/Bugwood_18 - wilting/yellowing, no focal lesion

**Conclusion:** The test image shows a leaf (on a gray CDDM-style background) with a single large dark brown/gray lesion featuring **clear concentric rings** and adjacent yellowing. This is the definitive signature of Early Blight (Alternaria solani). No other candidate class shows this concentric ring (target) pattern. The CDDM-style background confirms it's from the same dataset as the Early Blight CDDM references.
